::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Cannot figure out a second order lineary differential equation with initial values](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1117467/cannot-figure-out-a-second-order-lineary-differential-equation-with-initial-valu), asked by [Cheiron](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/64778/cheiron) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-01-24; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I got the following question:
>
> Solve the following initial value problem:
> $y(0) = 0$, $y'(0) = 1$, $$y'' + 10y' + 25y = 0$$
>
> So I started with getting the general solution:
> $$y(x) = C_1e^{-5x} + xC_2e^{-5x}$$
> And then calculating the derative while i am at it:
> $$y'(x) = -5C_1e^{-5x} -5C_2xe^{-5x}$$
> After filling in the conditions, the solution should be:
> $y = xe^{-5x}$. And that is where I get stuck: I do not get that answer.
>
> First i fill in condition y(0) = 0
> $$0 = C_1*1 + 0 => C_1 = 0$$
> And then y'(0) = 1:
> $$1 = -5C_1*1 + 0 => C_1 = -1/5$$
> Which is, obviously incorrect. Where did I make the mistake? How do I solve this?
:::

Your mistake is in this line:
$$y'(x) = -5C_1e^{-5x} -5C_2xe^{-5x} \color{red}{+C_2 e^{-5x}}$$
by the product rule.
